title: api: standardize rate-limit semantics, idempotency and retry-after for streaming & function calls (openai-compat)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Streaming endpoints and the OpenAI-compat adapter returned inconsistent rate-limit headers and error bodies which caused client SDKs and product code to mis-handle 429s and reconnect logic. In particular: 1) streaming SSE/WebSocket flows sometimes emitted only a final error frame without standard Retry-After/X-RateLimit headers; 2) function/tool-calling requests could accept Idempotency-Key but behavior on partial/broken streams was undefined; 3) Retry-After was returned as HTTP-date in some flows and seconds in others, causing SDKs to incorrectly backoff. This PR standardizes rate-limit semantics across normal and streaming responses, unifies idempotency key handling for OpenAI-compat endpoints, and adds clearer error payloads. Summary of changes: centralized RateLimitNormalizer middleware that ensures all 429 responses include Retry-After (seconds) and X-RateLimit-{Limit,Remaining,Reset} when available; updated openai_compat adapter to map internal rate-limit metrics to OpenAI-compatible headers and to include a structured error body {"error":{"message","type","param","code","retry_after"}}; implemented stream-safe error frames for SSE and WebSocket flows so that streaming errors include the same standard metadata (headers are emitted on connection close and an explicit final error event/frame is sent); clarified idempotency semantics: Idempotency-Key header is honored for all non-idempotent endpoints including streaming function calls; if a stream fails before any event is emitted, the request is retried according to idempotency rules; if partial content was delivered, the server marks the idempotency key as "incomplete" and returns 409 with guidance to the client. Backwards compatibility: the middleware defaults to preserve existing behavior when headers are absent and provides a feature flag to enable strict OpenAI-compat mapping for private deployments. Testing: unit tests for middleware, integration tests for SSE/WebSocket error frames and function-calling workflows, end-to-end flaky streaming reconnection scenarios. Rollout: feature-flagged rollout to staging, monitor rate-limit metrics and SDK error-tally. Checklist: - [x] Middleware implementation - [x] OpenAI-compat adapter mapping - [x] Streaming error-frame support - [x] Tests (unit/integration/e2e) - [x] Docs and migration notes - [x] Canary rollout plan
commits: 5 commits: 1) Add RateLimitNormalizer middleware and tests; 2) Map internal RL metrics to OpenAI headers in openai_compat adapter; 3) Implement streaming error-frame support (SSE/WebSocket) and tests; 4) Idempotency handling for streaming/function calls; 5) Docs and changelog updates
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Please confirm that the X-RateLimit-Reset is always seconds-since-epoch and never an HTTP-date; we had clients parsing both forms before. Author: confirmed and fixed mapping to seconds-since-epoch for Reset. Lina Chen: Add metrics for dropped streaming error frames and ensure we emit a tracing span with request_id and idempotency_key. Author: added counters and tracing spans in RateLimitNormalizer and streaming layer. Marco Rossi: Concern about behavior for dedicated/private installs with old proxies that strip custom headers; requested a fallback in the adapter body. Author: added a fallback body field 'retry_after' inside the JSON error payload when headers are absent so clients can rely on the body. CI: initial run failed lint in adapter and a flaky streaming test; fixes applied and tests re-run. Final: Diego approved, Lina approved, Marco approved.
release_notes: Standardized rate-limit and idempotency semantics across streaming and non-streaming endpoints. OpenAI-compat adapter now emits Retry-After (seconds), X-RateLimit-{Limit,Remaining,Reset} and a consistent structured error body. Idempotency-Key behavior clarified for streaming/function-calling: retries allowed for no-output failures, partial-output returns 409 with guidance. Feature-flagged rollout for private installs.
notes_for_engineering: Monitoring: watch rate_limit/429_count, streaming/error_frame_dropped, idempotency/partial_conflicts. Suggest SDK teams add support for JSON error bodies with retry_after and for final error frames on streams. Backwards compatibility: if clients only read headers, they will continue to function; advise updating to parse body fallback for private deployments behind proxies.
